summary: This is a complete Hangman game implementation. A player guesses letters to figure out a hidden word, getting 5 wrong guesses before losing. The game loops until the player chooses to quit, and it includes visual feedback showing the hangman drawing getting progressively worse with each wrong guess.

explanations.9: This keeps asking for input in a loop until the user enters either 'y' or 'n' (case-insensitive), rejecting any other input.
explanations.19: This creates a string of underscores as long as the secret word, representing the unrevealed letters the player will gradually fill in.
explanations.22: Converting the word to a list of letters makes it easier to remove letters as the player guesses them correctly.
explanations.25: .strip() removes any accidental whitespace the user might have typed before or after their letter.
explanations.26: This validates that the user entered exactly one character—rejecting empty input or multiple letters.
explanations.30: This checks if the player already guessed this letter before, to avoid penalizing them twice for the same wrong guess.
explanations.35: .remove() deletes only the first occurrence of the guessed letter from the letters list, which is used later to detect when the word is complete.
explanations.36: .find() locates the position of the guessed letter in the word so we know where to reveal it in the display.
explanations.37: This reconstructs the display string by inserting the correctly guessed letter at the position it was found.
explanations.40: Only wrong guesses get added to the guessed list; correct guesses are tracked differently via the letters list.
explanations.113: Comparing the display string to the original word tells us if all letters have been revealed—meaning the player won.
explanations.125: This clears the terminal screen; it uses 'cls' on Windows or 'clear' on Unix-based systems.
explanations.144: random.choice() picks one word at random from the list for each new game.
explanations.152: This Python idiom ensures play_hangman() only runs if this file is executed directly, not if it's imported elsewhere.
